Definition: a gift (as the price of harlotry or idolatry)
BiblicalUsage: ʼEthnan is the hire of a harlot — the price paid for prostitution, named as a gift that must never be brought into God's house. Moses forbids bringing the hire of a whore into the house of the LORD, and the prophets use the word for Israel's payment to her lovers. It is money earned by unfaithfulness, and God will not take it as an offering.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʼethnan shows how seriously God takes the source of what we offer Him: a gift bought with unfaithfulness is no gift at all. I hold that the warning still stands — what I bring to God must come from a faithful life, not merely a full hand.
